content:
marta: heads-up — last night's nightly eval on `redwood/quant-v2` had ~18% failures on the prompt set, intermittent. looks like prompt text is getting corrupted or interleaved across examples. not a model regression pattern.
kevin: can you paste a failing snippet and any traceback?
marta: sure. here's the most common stack we saw in the logs:
```
PromptCache.load(): reading /tmp/eval_cache.pkl
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "harness/runner.py", line 212, in run_case
    prompt = cache.get(case_id)
  File "harness/cache.py", line 87, in get
    obj = pickle.loads(data)
_pickle.UnpicklingError: unpickling stack underflow
```
marta: and the generated output for a failing case often contains fragments from previous prompts, e.g. "...Tell me a recipe for apple pie. \nQ: What is Newton's second law? A: Force = mass\n..." — so prompts are being concatenated or corrupted.
jen: that strongly smells like concurrent writes to the same cache file or a write/read race across worker processes. are we using multiprocessing with spawn/forkserver? what temp filename pattern do we use?
marta: harness spawns workers via `multiprocessing.Pool` with start method `spawn`. cache uses a simple file per run: `/tmp/eval_cache_{shard}.pkl`. We thought shard==worker_id but the harness reuses shard ids across retries, and the worker subprocess may reopen the same file concurrently.
ryan: repro idea: run `pytest tests/evals::test_failure --count=100 -k nightly` in loop with 8 workers, should flip. quick confirm: i reproduced locally with 4 workers, 1/10 runs fail with unpickling error.
kevin: quick mitigation: stop sharing a single pkl blob across processes. options:
  - write per-worker cache files (include pid + uuid) and atomic replace
  - use sqlite (single-writer, WAL) or tiny leveldb per run
  - avoid pickle and use newline-delimited JSON records + line-atomic append + fsync
jen: I'd prefer JSONL for simplicity; pickle isn't safe for concurrent writes and it's black-box when corrupted. plus it's easier to grep. but JSON may be slower; for nightly it should be fine.
marta: patch idea in PR: when writing cache, use `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False)` + `os.replace(tmp, final)` and make filenames include worker pid+uuid. also add retry/backoff when loading unpickling error and fallback to re-generating prompt. propose to add a small recovery: on UnpicklingError treat as cache-miss (log once) to avoid failing whole eval run.
kevin: also add file locking during write (fcntl) as belt-and-suspenders for platforms that support it.
ryan: test matrix: run nightly harness with 12 workers for 48h in CI matrix, validate no UnpicklingError traces and confirm distributions of failing cases drop to baseline.
eval-bot: nightly-eval: https://ci.redwood.com/nightly/1861239876 — failing runs 18% -> after patch retest.
marta: i'll open the PR today with the JSONL switch + crash-to-cache-miss fallback. tagging @kevin @jen for review. :thumbsup:
kevin: ack, will review and add fcntl wrapper. if we still have flakiness after that we should consider switching harness to an IPC actor that owns the cache.
jen: thanks — good catch, this explains why failures were nondeterministic and not model-quality related.
